claims.text: Unmodified TC4 is Ti6Al4V with a dual-phase α+β microstructure.
The α+β microstructure of TC4 provides a beneficial strength-to-weight ratio and fatigue properties.
TC4 should be gas nitrided in a nitrogen-rich atmosphere, such as N2-H2, at approximately 850°C for four hours and then cooled under controlled conditions.
Gas nitriding of TC4 under the proposed conditions will form a TiN-rich surface layer.
The resulting TiN-rich layer will be nanocrystalline, uniformly adherent, finely dispersed, of controlled thickness, and low in residual stress.
Controlled cooling can manage the thickness and uniformity of the nitride layer.
Nitrogen will diffuse into the TC4 surface and react with titanium to form TiN precipitates.
Finely dispersed TiN precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion and thereby increase surface hardness.
The TiN-containing surface layer will resist plowing during contact and thereby improve wear resistance.
The proposed surface treatment will leave the underlying α+β microstructure largely intact.
Nitrided TC4 will have approximately 40–60% greater surface hardness than untreated TC4.
Nitrided TC4 will exhibit markedly lower wear volume than untreated TC4 under high-contact-stress conditions.
The proposed nitriding treatment will preserve TC4's beneficial ductility and fatigue performance.
Untreated TC4 has relatively low hardness and poor friction and wear properties under extreme-service conditions.
The benefits of the proposed treatment are expected under high-contact-stress and extreme-service conditions.
The treatment outcome will be sensitive to precise control of nitriding parameters and cooling rate.
The nitride layer may suffer brittleness, cracking, adhesion loss, or spallation under cyclic loading.
The exact hardness and wear improvements will depend on fine-tuning the process parameters.
Failure to obtain at least a 30% hardness increase or a 30% wear-volume reduction, or observation of pronounced brittle failure under cyclic loading, will falsify the hypothesis.
